summary: A local news feature on the city's push toward green public transportation, built from interviews with City Council Member Roberta Wallace, activist Dr. Julian Kershaw, and commuter Grace Thompson. It covers fleet retrofits and new electric buses, a reported 10% drop in transport emissions, the Charge Up Program for EV charging, community Ride Green Days, and challenges such as funding, infrastructure and car culture. It closes with upcoming plans and effects on urban planning.
one_line: Interviews with officials, an activist and a commuter show how the city's green transit programs are cutting emissions while facing funding and infrastructure hurdles.
key_facts: City Council Member Roberta Wallace was interviewed on September 5th, 2023 and is described as a well-known advocate for sustainable public transport.
Wallace's twofold strategy is retrofitting existing fleets with more efficient engines and power systems while adding newer, cleaner electric and hybrid models.
Funding and public perception were cited as significant challenges; Wallace said the city uses government grants and partnerships with private clean-energy firms.
Dr. Julian Kershaw, founder of the 'Green Wheels Movement', said that on September 20th the city reached a 10% decrease in transport-sector emissions compared to the previous year.
Kershaw said the initiatives include tax incentives for regular green transit users and educational campaigns in schools and local communities.
On September 30th the 'Green Line Initiative' launched a new fleet of electric buses with Wi-Fi, charging stations and real-time location updates.
The 'Charge Up Program', introduced October 15th, aims to install 500 new EV charging points by the end of 2024.
Wallace said that shifting car culture is "as much a cultural transition as it is a technological one."
'Ride Green Days' offer free public transit and have been popular with young riders; the latest took place October 29th.
Commuter Grace Thompson called the new buses "a complete turnaround," saying they are clean and quiet and let her charge her phone.
Upcoming projects include expanding bike lanes, considering incentives for remote work, and developing a user-friendly public transport app with tech companies.
New housing development proposals now require easy access to public transit, and businesses are exploring employee shuttle services.
